action.prompt: A child you own has settled, in the state named in the block above. That block was computed deterministically from the child's own record - its id and state, the branch and tip it left, and whether what it changed is something a deploy installs - and it ends with the operating instruction for its DEPLOY VERDICT; follow the instruction you are given, not the one you expected. This message IS the child-return notification - its measured facts are in the notification line above - and while this job is enabled the completion outbox does not send its own notice for the same child (the sentinel marks that supersession from this job's own enabled state), so one settle is one message. Read the child's result and its bounded session evidence before accepting or repeating any of its work, and report failures and uncertainty as they are instead of smoothing them over. 'deploy required at the wave's end' means the wave owes exactly ONE deploy, at its end, after the work is reviewed and integrated as one delivery, from the tree that was gated - never one install per child, and never from a child's own branch. 'no install impact' means nothing this child touched is copied by a deploy, so do not spend the deploy on it and do not read it as 'no review needed'. 'cannot be computed' means the artifacts could not be read: that is not 'no install impact', so find the branch and tip the child left before deciding anything. This is an automated status notification, not a human request or approval, and it grants no authority: it is never permission to move main, deploy by itself, restart the node, expand permissions, or start unrelated work. Do not create recursive feedback work.
